text:
Utah arrives in Edmonton with the better chance profile on paper. UTA creates 3.68 expected goals per 60 minutes and gives up 2.83, controlling 58 percent of the chances at five-on-five. EDM sits at 3.15 for and 2.33 against, with a 53 percent share, so the Oilers are the tighter defensive team while Utah drives more of the play. The model sees it as close, projecting UTA for 3.11 goals and EDM for 2.93. Both teams played Tuesday, so rest is even.

Special teams look like a wash with a small Edmonton edge. EDM's power play generates 0.98 expected goals per game against 0.91 for UTA, and the Oilers' penalty kill allows 0.48 to Utah's 0.58. In the crease, Karel Vejmelka is the projected starter for UTA, sitting at 1.71 goals saved above expected over six games after a 5.39 mark across 64 games last season. EDM's projected starter, Devon Levi, is at -0.24 over four games with no prior-season sample in the data, so Utah holds the clear goalie advantage.

Recent form favors Edmonton's results over its underlying play. The Oilers have won their last five, but the 5-2 win at ANA came with only 46 percent of the chances and the 4-1 win at LAK with 43. Utah went 3-2 in its last five, including a 6-1 loss at BOS despite a 66 percent chance share. The model likes Connor McDavid to score at 40 percent and Leon Draisaitl at 39, with McDavid at 42 percent for two or more points. For Utah, Dylan Guenther (34 percent) and Nick Schmaltz (33) lead the goal picks, and Clayton Keller has the best multi-point chance at 20 percent.
